qualifying_findings.title: AI Engine WordPress MCP OAuth client registration lacks authorization
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: GitHub Advisory Database high-severity unreviewed CVE record with public WordPress plugin source and release references
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: AI Engine versions through 3.8.6 register the MCP OAuth 2.1 dynamic-client-registration endpoint with an always-allow permission callback. The record says an unauthenticated attacker can register a client using an attacker-controlled redirect URI and, after administrator consent, obtain an administrator-bound MCP token; the advisory also identifies absent anti-framing controls as enabling clickjacking of that consent step.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: AI Engine WordPress plugin through 3.8.6; MCP OAuth dynamic client registration and administrator consent boundary. The referenced 3.8.7 tag is a likely fix boundary that must be confirmed from maintainer release material during ingest.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: It joins an MCP client-registration flaw to delegated administrator authority: consent and token binding can turn a public registration endpoint into administrator-level MCP tool access.

upstream_routing.entity_owner: ai-wiki owns broad AI Engine, WordPress, MCP, and OAuth entity coverage.
upstream_routing.security_wiki_retention: Retain the authorization, redirect-URI, consent-clickjacking, token-binding, and MCP tool-authority implication here.

qualifying_findings.confidence: high for disclosure timing and vulnerability description; medium for fixed-version wording pending an explicit maintainer security release note.
follow_up_actions: Verify the maintained fixed release and whether 3.8.7 fully remediates all cited boundaries before durable synthesis.
Avoid treating administrator approval as proof that a registered OAuth client is trustworthy.

qualifying_findings.title: Kubeflow Pipelines run-log endpoint permits cross-run log access
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: GitHub-reviewed high-severity maintainer advisory with linked fix pull request, commit, and release
security_topics: AI runtime and cloud deployment security
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: Kubeflow Pipelines' run-log handler retrieved live or archived logs without authorizing the caller against the selected run. The advisory says a caller able to reach the backend and possessing a victim run ID plus a suitable pod or node identifier could read logs, including an unrelated pod's main-container logs under stated conditions; those logs can contain sensitive workload data or credentials.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Kubeflow Pipelines API server versions through 2.17.3; package range below 0.0.0-20260904182349-be4723e33727. The advisory directs upgrade to 2.18.0 and says the fix authorizes the readLog verb and checks the pipeline/runid label for live logs.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Shared ML-pipeline infrastructure must bind log access to the pipeline run, not merely to backend reachability. Logs are a frequent AI data and credential leakage boundary.

upstream_routing.entity_owner: ai-wiki owns broad Kubeflow and pipeline-platform entity coverage.
upstream_routing.security_wiki_retention: Retain the run-scoped authorization, pod/run identity check, log-data exposure, and remediation evidence here.

qualifying_findings.confidence: high; the advisory is GitHub reviewed, gives exact timestamps, affected boundaries, mitigation, and release linkage.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, keep this distinct from the same-release archive-upload denial-of-service finding.
Confirm any deployment-specific custom Kubernetes role grants after upgrading.

qualifying_findings.title: Kubeflow Pipelines archive upload can cause decompression-amplification denial of service
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: GitHub-reviewed high-severity maintainer advisory with linked remediation pull requests and product release
security_topics: AI runtime and cloud deployment security
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: Kubeflow Pipelines decompressed uploaded ZIP or gzip-compressed tar pipeline archives without adequate expansion bounds before namespace authorization. The advisory says a small archive can consume disproportionate API-server memory and interrupt service; it describes 2.18.0 changes that bound compressed input, extracted pipeline data, and tar traversal budgets.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Kubeflow Pipelines API server versions through 2.17.3; pipeline and pipeline-version upload processing. The advisory directs upgrade to 2.18.0 and advises restricting upload/import reachability plus applying request and resource limits until upgraded.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: ML pipeline archives are AI deployment artifacts. This demonstrates that authorization sequencing and resource budgets are release-gate controls, not merely performance settings.

upstream_routing.entity_owner: ai-wiki owns broad Kubeflow and ML-pipeline coverage.
upstream_routing.security_wiki_retention: Retain the decompression-amplification boundary, authorization ordering, artifact-upload controls, and fixed release here.

qualifying_findings.confidence: high for the advisory and mitigation; deployment-specific resource exhaustion depends on configured limits and concurrent activity, as the advisory notes.
follow_up_actions: Keep this as a separate availability and artifact-boundary record from CVE-2026-118759.
Check deployment-level request, disk, CPU, and concurrency limits rather than relying only on compressed-upload size.

qualifying_findings.title: DeepInfer unauthenticated profiling endpoint permits path traversal and trace-file writes
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Public CVE record assigned by VulnCheck and mirrored in the GitHub Advisory Database; linked product source and patch pull request
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: DeepInfer through 0.1.0 exposes an unauthenticated /profile endpoint whose output_dir parameter permits path traversal. The public record says an attacker can create arbitrary directories and write Chrome trace files, with disk or inode exhaustion and filesystem-oracle behavior possible through error messages.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: deepseek-ai/DeepInfer through 0.1.0; unauthenticated /profile output_dir handling. The public record links pull request 242 but does not name a released fixed version.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Inference and profiling surfaces are part of the AI runtime attack surface. An unauthenticated diagnostic endpoint can bridge remote access to host filesystem effects and denial of service.

upstream_routing.entity_owner: ai-wiki owns broad DeepInfer and DeepSeek-AI entity coverage.
upstream_routing.security_wiki_retention: Retain the unauthenticated profiling-service, filesystem traversal, trace-output, and remediation-gap analysis here.

qualifying_findings.confidence: medium-high: precise same-day CVE and advisory timestamps plus linked source evidence are available, but no maintained fixed release is identified in the public record.
follow_up_actions: Reconcile pull request 242 with a maintainer-tagged release before declaring an upgrade target.
Restrict or disable unauthenticated profiling endpoints pending a verified fix.
